title: The wrinkles come back

rights.source: OpenAI image generation; exact prompt in public/assets/bath-wrinkle/storybook-prompt.txt

question: Do your bath wrinkles make a new pattern every time?
answer: Some of the same lines return.
explanation: Researchers photographed the same fingertips after two soaks at least a day apart. The skin had smoothed out between soaks, but major wrinkles returned in similar places and directions.
qualification: This preliminary 2025 study involved three adults. Some wrinkles differed between soaks.
whyCare: You’ve seen your fingers prune. Have you ever looked closely at the lines?

share.question: Do your bath wrinkles make a new pattern every time?
share.description: What happens to your fingertip wrinkles when you soak your hands again?

evidence.scope: Three adults, ages 19–22; five right-hand fingers each.
evidence.denominator: Three people observed at two time points; repeated wrinkle measurements are not independent participants.
evidence.methodology: Laytin and German, §§2–3.3 and Figure 3. Two 30-minute immersions at 40°C, at least 24 hours apart. Researchers paired wrinkles and compared orientations. Exact calendar dates unspecified. Small sample and manual pairing limit generalization. No calculation; blood-vessel mapping remains a hypothesis.

sources.label: Laytin and German (2025): methods, limitations and Figure 3
Primary paper, publisher-layout PDF hosted by Newswise

editorial.reviewFormat: Selected memory drawing exercise in a hand-painted animated bath: inspect invented creases on an illustrated fingertip, drain the water, draw from memory, and uncover the original. Reduced-motion and skip-drawing alternatives. No score or claim that the exercise measures wrinkle recurrence.
